answer: The exact answer is the finite determinantal formula Δ_b = 4g−3 + rank_C A_S(b) − rank_C A_O(b) − rank_C A_L(b), with ranks evaluated at the given vector b. Define N=4g−3, B=4g, s(t)=(1−t^(4g+2))^(1/2), a(t)=−(1/2)t^(−2g+2)s(t), and P(t,w)=1−k t^k φ_b(t)w^k. For M≥0 let B(M)={t^(−2i): i≥0, 2i≤M} ∪ {t^(−2i−2g−1)s(t): i≥0, 2i+2g+1≤M}. All series below are truncated modulo w^N, and a column is its coefficient vector in the specified rows. A_O and A_L have rows (m,e) with 0≤m<N and −B−3m≤e<0. For each 0≤n<N, A_O has columns f(t)t^n w^n P^(−n/k), for f∈B(4n+B), and A_L has columns f(t)a(t)t^n w^n P^(1−n/k), for f∈B(4n+B−2g+2). A_S has rows (h,m,e) with 0≤m<N and 1−B−3m≤e<0, and rows (v,m,e) with 0≤m<N and −B−3m≤e<0. Its columns, written as (horizontal,vertical) pairs, are (0, f(t)t^n w^n P^(1−n/k)) for f∈B(4n+B), and (f(t)a(t)t^n w^n P^(−n/k), f(t)a(t)t^n w^n P^(−n/k)(−t^(−1)−t^k φ_b′(t)w^k)) for f∈B(4n+B−2g+1), for every 0≤n<N. This formula applies to every allowed coefficient vector, including vectors with vanishing components.
